title: Low-precision quantization without quality loss
bottleneck: Pushing models below 4-bit precision — necessary for affordable deployment — degrades reasoning quality unpredictably: outliers in activations break naive quantization, and degradation concentrates in exactly the complex reasoning tasks users care about. Per-layer dynamic scaling and new formats help but add complexity, and aggressive quantization can silently lobotomize a model while headline benchmarks look fine. Calibration data for quantization rarely matches deployment distributions, so real-world degradation exceeds lab measurements.
why_it_blocks: The gap between runs-on-available-hardware and still-smart is decided by quantization. Bad quantization wastes the entire training investment. Every serving dollar saved by quantization is paid in capability; the frontier of the tradeoff is unmapped territory.
current_state: FP8 is now standard on H100/B200 GPUs with negligible loss; sub-4-bit remains a quality cliff for reasoning-heavy workloads.
